Access to such eigenpairs is essential for studying non-equilibrium many-body physics, but is hindered by the exponential growth of Hilbert-space dimension. POLFED addresses this challenge through a polynomial spectral transformation evaluated on the fly within a Lanczos iteration, preserving Hamiltonian sparsity and substantially reducing memory costs compared to other diagonalization methods. The package supports flexible energy targeting, automatic optimization of the spectral mapping for structured Hamiltonians, and GPU acceleration, which is particularly effective since the dominant computational cost reduces to repeated sparse matrix-vector multiplications. Benchmarks on disordered spin-chain and fermionic models demonstrate access to larger system sizes than alternative approaches, and CPU--GPU comparisons confirm significant speedups. In particular, we also provide code for constructing the quantum sun model Hamiltonian, a toy model of a many-body ergodicity-breaking transition. While our focus is on many-body Hamiltonians, Polfed$.$jl may be applied to any large sparse matrix.
item.dc:creator: Rok Pintar, Konrad Pawlik, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Miroslav Hopjan, Jan \v{S}untajs, Jakub Zakrzewski, Piotr Sierant, Lev Vidmar

item.title: Link length and energy fluctuations in extensible freely jointed chains
item.description: arXiv:2605.12333v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The freely jointed chain is often applied to model the thermodynamics of single polymer chains, but the traditional formulation of the model lacks internal energy changes due to bond stretching. For this reason, the extensible freely jointed chain model includes a potential energy function, typically harmonic, that governs the length of each link in the chain. Among the other quantities of interest that are subject to thermal fluctuations, these link lengths and energies too fluctuate about their ensemble average values. Since a plethora of models for polymer chains and networks incorporate chain dissociation as a function of either link length or energy, these fluctuations are crucial to understand and quantify. Motivated by this fact, fluctuations in link length and energy are analyzed within a freely jointed chain under an applied force. These fluctuations are quantified through their average values, standard deviations, and probability distributions. Across all values, asymptotically correct analytic relations and their less ergonomic exact counterparts are introduced. The asymptotic relations are verified to be accurate through direct comparison and to be correct within transcendentally small terms through error analysis. In certain cases, the fluctuations are shown to be approximately normally distributed. Hereafter, model components predicated on link length or energy ought to account for these fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Michael R. Buche

item.title: Boltzmann-like occupation of nonequilibrium steady states on dense disordered networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.14542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central problem in statistical physics is to extend the Boltzmann distribution to nonequilibrium steady states (NESS). We prove that NESS on large dense disordered networks have Boltzmann-like occupation despite extensive entropy production. One consequence is that such NESS can conceal their nonequilibrium nature from measurements of static response to energy perturbations. We further prove that the active-matter heuristic of "low rattling" is asymptotically exact for these NESS. Intuitively, they spend a greater fraction of their time in states they leave more slowly. We show that rattling effectively extends the Boltzmann distribution to such NESS, as well as the broader class of "equiaccessible" steady states, which play a role in our analysis akin to that of equilibrium in linear response.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Calvert

item.title: Altered temporal scaling of semantic similarity fluctuations in psychosis
item.description: arXiv:2606.23043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scale-free temporal organization, in which fluctuations show similar statistical structures across timescales, is a feature of many complex systems considered to support optimal functioning. Alterations of such scaling have been reported in several pathologies, but whether comparable alterations characterize the temporal organization of language remains largely unexplored. We address this question in the domain of psychosis, where language anomalies are pervasively documented. Specifically, we apply detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) to quantify temporal scaling in Qwen3-derived continuous cosine similarity time series, capturing trajectories through semantic space computed from transcripts of picture descriptions across three independent datasets. DFA scaling exponents {\alpha} were extracted to characterize the strength of long-range temporal correlations. Across all datasets, patients exhibited significantly elevated {\alpha} relative to controls, indicating increased temporal persistence in semantic fluctuations. This analysis opens a window into the multi-timescale organization of meaning as it unfolds in discourse and reveals a signature of altered temporal scaling. This alteration parallels known departures from critical scaling in brain dynamics in psychosis, suggesting the exploration of possible links between these two.
item.dc:creator: Paola Moreno Ancalmo, Irem Topal, Emre Bora, Rieke Roxanne M\"ulfarth, Svenja Seuffert, Tilo Kircher, Frederike Stein, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen

item.title: Modified Family-Vicsek Scaling and Probability Distributions for Brownian Castle Interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.13922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Brownian Castle is a new interface growth model that is a variation on the well-known ballistic deposition model that results in an entirely new universality class. We present numerical verification that the interface width for BC interfaces displays modified Family-Vicsek scaling properties up to finite size corrections. Specifically, we find a growth exponent of $\beta=0.470 \pm 0.012$ and a roughness exponent of $\alpha=1.01 \pm 0.018$. The scaling is modified at short times with a size scaling exponent that described the early time dependence of interface width on length. The probability distribution of heights for the BC interface shows significant deviations from simple Gaussian behavior and the probability distribution of height changes shows a Cauchy-Lorentz form consistent with expectations for a process involving relatively large jumps.
item.dc:creator: Noah Sublett, Charles Sutton, Benjamin Long, Daniel B. Dougherty

item.title: Ensemble theory of thermodiffusion
item.description: arXiv:2607.27839v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Heat flow sustained by a temperature difference generates a gradient of matter as observed, for example, in atomistic simulations of hard-core gases. We use path-ensemble theory to represent the coupled thermal and diffusive transport by dynamics on a graph. Calibrated from a single equilibrium simulation, this model accurately predicts nonequilibrium mass distribution in a hard-core gas across a wide range of applied temperature gradients. It also enables estimation of transport properties, such as the Soret coefficient, using analytical expressions.
item.dc:creator: R. Belousov, J. Elliott, A. Erzberger

item.title: MUTACO: Simulator-Efficient Response Matching in Stochastic Nonlinear Systems via Compatibility-Aware Sequential Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.04619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many physical inverse problems are mediated by expensive stochastic simulators for which response gradients, adjoint sensitivities, or a differentiable simulator interface are unavailable. We introduce \emph{Multiple Target-based Confident Acquisition} (MUTACO), an uncertainty-aware sequential-design method for response matching that requires only noisy forward evaluations and learns the multicomponent response together with its predictive uncertainty. We develop and evaluate MUTACO using a heterogeneous network of stochastic phase oscillators. The inverse task is to infer statistical properties of the local potential and interactions from macroscopic rotation and synchronization curves under multiple driving conditions. Rather than requiring unique recovery of these statistical properties, MUTACO searches for parameter configurations whose predicted rotation and synchronization responses are compatible with the target response while accounting for predictive uncertainty. This response-centered formulation is appropriate when experimentally accessible observables characterize ensemble statistics rather than a particular microscopic realization. Under strictly limited simulation budgets, MUTACO achieves the lowest held-out response error among the tested adaptive-search, space-filling, and simulation-based inference methods, while also yielding lower parameter-recovery error than the compared methods. These results demonstrate that response-targeted sequential design is a simulator-efficient approach to inverse modeling from finite noisy forward evaluations and suggest broader applicability to stochastic physical systems with correlated multicomponent responses and weakly constrained parameter directions.
item.dc:creator: Ege Karadeniz, \.Ilter Onat Korkmaz, Umut Can Turhan, Cem Tekin, Ayd{\i}n Cem Keser

item.title: High-resolution mapping of the phase boundary of the honeycomb-lattice Blume--Capel ferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2610.11068v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a high-resolution numerical study of the spin-1 Blume-Capel ferromagnet on the honeycomb lattice ($z=3$). Using the Wang-Landau algorithm to estimate the joint density of states $\Omega(E_1,E_2)$ and field-mixing scaling, we map the first-order transition line and locate the tricritical point at $(\Delta_t,T_t)=[1.4820(2),0.4022(7)]$. Independent Metropolis histogram reweighting for $L=36$ and $48$ yields a crossing temperature near $0.4039$, consistent with the Wang-Landau extrapolation. The field-mixing parameter is $r=-1.585(19)$, while the coexistence-line slope gives $r=-1.587(5)$. Normalizing by the zero-temperature field $\Delta_0=zJ/2$, the results for honeycomb, square, and triangular lattices give $r/\Delta_0$ between $-1.057$ and $-1.067$, about 6% larger in magnitude than the mean-field value. Simple-cubic estimates are compatible with this range but do not resolve dimensionality dependence. Finite-size scaling yields $y_t=1.795(7)$, consistent with the tricritical Ising value $9/5$, while the fourth-order cumulant scaling agrees with $y_g=4/5$. Deep in the first-order regime, the cumulant approaches the two-phase limit $U_Q\to2/3$. Multicanonical simulations up to $L=64$ yield an interface tension exponent $\mu=1.265(26)$, consistent with the tricritical prediction $(d-1)/y_g=5/4$. We also map the continuous phase boundary, obtaining $T_c(\Delta=0)=1.157$, and identify crossover effects from Ising to tricritical scaling near the tricritical point.
item.dc:creator: Eluiz C. M. Filho, Claudio J. DaSilva

item.title: Competitive scaling of small-subsystem-optimization heuristics for LABS
item.description: arXiv:2610.14361v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) problem, often formulated as a spin-lattice energy-minimization problem, is a combinatorial optimization problem with a very rugged energy landscape. We demonstrate that iterative optimization of very small subsystems of n spins that are decoupled from the rest of the system achieves global optimization of LABS with a time-to-solution scaling that is competitive with heuristics that optimize the global system of N spins directly. Our isolated-subsystem heuristic with n = 4 achieves a time scaling of O(1.33^N ) on the interval N = [27, 60], while the current state-of-the-art classical and quantum scalings are respectively O(1.34^N ) and O(1.21^N ). Our results suggest that specialized optimization hardware with only small numbers of logical spins may be of practical relevance, and that quantum speedups demonstrated in the absence of decomposition may not provide a practical quantum advantage for large-scale problems that require decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Ginger E. Lau, Adil A. Gangat

item.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
item.description: arXiv:2610.19261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and scalar-valued free-probability methods, the most general case requires the more general framework of operator-valued free probability. We explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component and characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing.
item.dc:creator: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Wojciech Tarnowski, Sergey Denisov, Karol \.Zyczkowski

item.title: Maximum-Temperature Theorem for a Nanothermometer
item.description: arXiv:2610.24340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the quasi-steady temperature rise of a sensor of arbitrary shape and known thermometric volume $V_\mathrm{s}$, placed anywhere inside a region enclosed by an isothermal reference surface. The bound also requires the total heat power generated in the region $\dot{Q}_\mathrm{r}$ and a lower bound on its thermal conductivity $\kappa_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal {V}_{\mathrm{r}}}}$. It is otherwise independent of the heat-source distribution, domain shape, and source--sensor distance. For $\dot Q_\mathrm{r}=50~\mathrm{pW}$, $\kappa_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}} =0.1~\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $V_{\mathrm s}$ equal to the volume of a $60~\mathrm{nm}$-diameter sphere, the theorem permits a maximum temperature rise of approximately $2~\mathrm{mK}$. Neither source localization nor uncertain source--sensor separation can therefore account for reported kelvin-scale intracellular readings under steady-state heat conduction. The result applies to sensors based on nanodiamonds, upconversion nanoparticles, fluorescent polymer beads, and core--shell quantum dots.
item.dc:creator: Taras Plakhotnik

item.title: Scaling Dimensions and Two-Point Amplitudes from Operator Covariance Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.24943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The long distance behavior of two-point functions of critical lattice statistical mechanics models depend on detailed information of the underlying quantum field theory. Yet these universal properties can be difficult to extract because generic lattice operators couple to the infinite hierarchy of continuum scaling operators with unknown coefficients. Recently in Physical Review E 114, 024146 (2026), one approach to disentangle some of this information was proposed using the eigen-decomposition of the operator covariance matrix constructed from cross correlations of a finite set of $N_\ell$ lattice operators. In this work we analyze this method in detail. We provide an explicit proof that under the assumption of scale invariance the leading decay of the eigenvalues are controlled by the smallest $N_\ell$ scaling dimensions, even after taking irrelevant perturbations into account. Based on this understanding, we propose a new method by which the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix can be used to construct the amplitudes of the continuum two-point correlation functions. This allows for a complete determination of the structure of the continuum two-point functions from the lattice covariance matrix. We demonstrate our ideas both on synthetic data sets (drawn from the scaling hypothesis) and numerically exact data for the two dimensional Ising model.
item.dc:creator: You-Chiuan Chen, Ribhu K. Kaul

item.title: A Transport-Information Framework for Continuous-Fiber-Aligned Coarse-Graining Representation Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.27811v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider representation sets of interest whose elements are associated with continuous realizations related to them through coarse-graining (CG). CG can be regarded as an operation that reduces a representation by discarding information that is not retained in its output. However, a systematic description of the information structure associated with CG in general remains to be established. Here, we propose a transport-information framework for continuous-fiber-aligned representation sets, in which each representation is associated with a continuous realization through a fiber structure, with CG defining the projection onto the representation. Within this framework, CG is described through a local-map operation that transports continuous probability mass onto representative points. The resulting transport cost is expressed as the contraction of the second-moment structure of the underlying continuous representation with the transport metric. Building on the previously proposed framework of unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), this construction provides a non-arbitrary information-theoretic interpretation of the CG-associated transport cost in terms of information indistinguishability, quantified by an expected second-order structure on statistical manifold associated with the CG geometry. We also show that the proposed framework can also be naturally extended to the CG of the discrete measures themselves. The present framework provides a basis for describing information costs associated with individual CG operations and for comparing representation sets while accounting for their underlying continuous realizations.
item.dc:creator: Koretaka Yuge

item.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.35973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed before a global average can be inferred with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ uniformly sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. The law of total variance exposes a second error, the floor $R_n$, which arises because the observed configuration is a single draw from equilibrium: no relative tolerance below $\kappa\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle we derive $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$ and show that the posterior remains calibrated. At the critical point of the two-dimensional Ising model the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$; its mean-field limit is $\sqrt{2}-1$. For correlated fields read by sensor networks, the usual $95\%$ interval covers the ensemble mean in $7\%$ of cases. Bounding the floor from one realisation, as in single-chain Monte Carlo diagnostics, requires an assumption on the decay of correlations.
item.dc:creator: Mihika Singhania

item.title: Stability reversal, activated escape, and mechanical response of negative-mobility particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.36884v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the fluctuations and response of particles in potential landscapes is a fundamental problem in nonequilibrium statistical physics. Here, we investigate how negative mobility reshapes the stochastic behavior of a particle moving in a mechanical potential landscape. We consider a one-dimensional overdamped particle subject to additive noise, with mobility that is negative at weak forces and positive at strong forces. In a potential well, negative mobility destabilizes the mechanical potential minimum and produces bimodal localization at two off-center positions. The same stability reversal transforms conventional Kramers escape from a potential well into a two-stage escape process involving an intermediate metastable state. When an additional spatially uniform force is applied, the mechanical perturbation translates rather than tilts the effective double well, yielding a positive response dominated at weak noise by intrawell relaxation, even though slow interwell switching dominates spontaneous positional fluctuations. These findings reveal how negative mobility reshapes the interplay among mechanical landscapes, stochastic stability, and response.
item.dc:creator: Junteng Li, Zhihong You

item.title: Dissipative Dynamical Phase Transition as a Complex Ising Model
item.description: arXiv:2412.09591v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a quantum dynamical phase transition induced by the competition between local unitary evolution and dissipation in a qubit chain with a strong, on-site $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. While the steady-state of this evolution is always maximally-mixed, we show that the dynamical behavior of certain non-local observables on the approach to this steady-state is dictated by a quantum Ising model with a complex transverse-field (cTFIM). A crucial feature of our mapping to the cTFIM is an extensive number of local, weak, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetries possessed by the dynamics, allowing us to investigate these observables analytically and uncover a dynamical phase transition as the relative rate of unitary evolution and dissipation is tuned. We show that the weak-dissipation limit corresponds to a cTFIM with a large magnitude of the imaginary transverse-field, for which the many-body "ground-state" (with smallest real eigenvalue) is gapless, exhibiting quasi-long-range correlations of the local magnetization with a continuously-varying exponent. Correspondingly, the dynamics of the non-local observables show oscillatory behavior with an amplitude decaying exponentially in time. The strong-dissipation limit corresponds to a gapped ferromagnetic phase of the cTFIM, and non-local observables show exponential decay on the approach to equilibrium. This transition in (1+1)-dimensions has a peculiar, "two-sided" nature appearing as either first- or second-order depending on the phase from which the transition is approached, an analytic result which is corroborated by numerical studies. In higher dimensions, we present a field-theoretic understanding of the first-order nature of this transition, when approaching from the ferromagnetic phase of the cTFIM, though the nature of the phase with large imaginary transverse-field remains to be understood.
item.dc:creator: Stephen W. Yan, Diego Barberena, Matthew P. A. Fisher, Sagar Vijay

item.title: Tight Generalization of Robertson-Type Uncertainty Relations
item.description: arXiv:2505.19861v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the tightest possible Robertson-type preparation uncertainty relation, which explicitly depends on the eigenvalues of the quantum state. The conventional constant $ \tfrac{1}{4} $ is replaced by the state-dependent coefficient \[ \frac{(\lambda_{\max} + \lambda_{\min})^2}{4(\lambda_{\max} - \lambda_{\min})^2}, \] where $ \lambda_{\max} $ and $\lambda_{\min}$ denote the largest and smallest eigenvalues of the density operator $ \rho $, respectively. We prove that this coefficient is optimal among all Robertson-type generalizations and does not admit further improvement. We also obtain a complete characterization of all nontrivial equality cases. Our relation becomes more pronounced as the quantum state becomes more mixed, capturing a trade-off in quantum uncertainty that the conventional Robertson's relation fails to detect. In addition, our result also provides a strict generalization of the Schr\"odinger's uncertainty relation, showing that the uncertainty trade-off is governed by the sum of the covariance term and a state-dependent improvement over the Robertson bound. As applications, we also refine error-disturbance trade-offs by incorporating spectral information of both the system and the measuring apparatus, thereby generalizing the Arthurs-Goodman and Ozawa inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Gen Kimura, Aina Mayumi, Haruki Yamashita

item.title: Entanglement Scaling of Motzkin Chains under Spiral Hamiltonian-path Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2506.02103v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate how a two-dimensional spatial embedding changes the entanglement observed across geometrically local bipartitions of a one-dimensional quantum spin chain. A $q$-deformed colored Motzkin chain is placed along a spiral-inspired Hamiltonian path that visits $N(L)=\Theta(L^2)$ sites of a square-lattice region while retaining a path interaction graph. Straight ambient-space cuts then correspond to unions of $\Theta(L)$ disconnected intervals in the chain ordering. We derive the scaling of a height-variation proxy for the leading color-pairing contribution and predict ambient-space entropy scaling proportional to $L^2$, $L$, and $O(1)$ for $q>1$, $q=1$, and $q<1$, respectively. We evaluate this proxy numerically using the matrix-product-state representation and verify its predicted finite-size scaling. The embedded and original Hamiltonians have exactly identical spectra and spectral gaps at fixed chain length. We also describe a sparse tensor-network representation and propose a two-chain junction extension. These results isolate the roles of interaction connectivity, spatial embedding, and subsystem geometry in entanglement scaling.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Zhang, Olai B. Mykland

item.title: Giant bubbles of Fisher zeros in the quantum XY chain
item.description: arXiv:2602.05899v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate an alternative approach based on a complex-valued inverse temperature and partition function to probe quantum phases of matter with nontrivial spectra and dynamics. It leverages thermofield dynamics (TFD) to quantitatively characterize quantum and thermal fluctuations, and exploit the correspondence between low-energy excitations and Fisher zeros. Using the quantum XY chain in an external field as a testbed, we show that the oscillatory gap behavior manifests as oscillations in the long-time dynamics of the TFD spectral form factor. We also identify giant bubbles, i.e. large-scale closed lines, of Fisher zeros near the gapless XX limit. They provide a characteristic energy scale that seems to contradict the predictions of the low energy theory of a featureless Luttinger liquid. We identify this energy scale and relate the motion of these giant bubbles with varying external field to the transfer of spectral weight from high to low energies. The deep connection between Fisher zeros, dynamics, and excitations opens up promising avenues for understanding the unconventional gap behaviors in strongly correlated many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Songtai Lv, Yang Liu, Erhai Zhao, Haiyuan Zou, Tao Xiang

item.title: Reducing the Computational Cost Scaling of Tensor Network Algorithms via Field-Programmable Gate Array Parallelism
item.description: arXiv:2602.05900v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Improving the computational efficiency of quantum many-body calculations from a hardware perspective remains a critical challenge. Although field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have recently been exploited to improve the computational scaling of algorithms such as Monte Carlo methods, their application to tensor network algorithms is still at an early stage. In this work, we propose a fine-grained parallel tensor network design based on FPGAs to substantially enhance the computational efficiency of two representative tensor network algorithms: the infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) and the higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG). By employing a quad-tile partitioning strategy to decompose tensor elements and map them onto hardware circuits, our approach effectively translates algorithmic computational complexity into scalable hardware resource utilization, enabling an extremely high degree of parallelism on FPGAs. Compared with conventional CPU-based implementations, our scheme exhibits superior scalability in computation time, reducing the bond-dimension scaling of the computational cost from $O(D_b^3)$ to $O(D_b)$ for iTEBD and from $O(D_b^6)$ to $O(D_b^2)$ for HOTRG. This work provides a theoretical foundation for future hardware implementations of large-scale tensor network computations.
item.dc:creator: Songtai Lv, Yang Liang, Rui Zhu, Qibin Zheng, Haiyuan Zou

item.title: Spontaneous Parity Breaking in Quantum Antiferromagnets on the Triangular Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2602.05901v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Frustration on the triangular lattice has long been a source of intriguing and often debated phases in many-body systems. Although symmetry analysis has been employed, the role of the seemingly trivial parity symmetry has received little attention. In the work described in this Letter, we show that phases induced by frustration are systematically shaped by an implicit rule of thumb associated with spontaneous parity breaking in weak longitudinal field. This principle enables us to anticipate and rationalize the regimes and conditions under which nontrivial phases emerge. For the spin-$S$ antiferromagnetic XXZ model, we demonstrate that a controversial parity-broken phase appears at intermediate values of $S$. In bilayer systems, enhanced frustration leads to additional phases, such as supersolids, whose properties can be classified by their characteristic parity features. Benefiting from our improved tensor network contraction techniques, we confirm these results through large-scale tensor-network calculations. This study offers an alternative viewpoint and a systematic approach for examining the interplay between spin, symmetry, and frustration in many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Songtai Lv, Yuchen Meng, Haiyuan Zou

item.title: Decoding cell signaling via optimal transport and information theory
item.description: arXiv:2602.18028v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cellular signal processing performs reliably despite molecular noise. Mutual information (MI) is widely used to quantify signaling fidelity, capturing how well outputs discriminate input states. However, it fails to capture whether the output preserves the statistical structure of the input, a property crucial in morphogen patterning and dose-dependent signaling. To address this gap, we introduce the 2-Wasserstein (2-WD) distance, which provides a geometric basis for comparing input and output distributions. We define MI as informational fidelity (INF) and the inverse of the 2-WD as geometric fidelity (GMF). Applying this dual-fidelity framework to canonical regulatory motifs under Gaussian channel approximation reveals topology-dependent trade-offs: coherent feed-forward loops can perform well in both dimensions, whereas feedback architectures reduce INF to enhance GMF. Experimental analysis of tumor necrosis factor signaling reveals dual-fidelity behavior qualitatively consistent with feedback regulation. RAS-MAPK data analysis further shows that jointly considering INF and GMF better characterizes intracellular signal relay than INF alone. Our results thus indicate that these signaling behaviors are not fully characterized by MI alone; instead, distributional correspondence provides a complementary dimension of signaling fidelity. Our study provides a practical framework for analyzing natural networks and guiding the design of task-specific synthetic circuits.
item.dc:creator: Mintu Nandi, Sosuke Ito

item.title: Partial Reversibility and Counterdiabatic Driving in Nearly Integrable Systems
item.description: arXiv:2602.22317v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Adiabatic (or reversible) processes are the key concept unifying our understanding of thermodynamics and dynamical systems. Reversibility in the thermodynamic sense is understood as entropy-preserving processes, such as in the idealized Carnot engine, whereas in integrable dynamical systems it is understood as the conservation of the action variables. Between these two idealized limits, however, things are much less clear. In this work, we study several toy models to assess the extent to which reversible processes are even possible in this regime. We then explore how the dissipative losses resulting from rapidly driving these kinds of systems can be fought by approximate counterdiabatic driving. Finally, we provide numerical evidence that much of the phenomenology should be the same for quantum many-body systems with large degeneracy in the presence of integrability breaking perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Rohan Banerjee, Shahyad Khamnei, Anatoli Polkovnikov, Stewart Morawetz

item.title: Universal purification dynamics in real non-unitary quantum processes
item.description: arXiv:2603.10751v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study purification dynamics in monitored quantum processes governed by ensembles of quantum circuits in different random-matrix symmetry classes. We analyze the universal aspects that emerge away from the measurement induced phase transition and inside the volume/weak measurement phase and in the scaling limit of large time and Hilbert space dimension. We present two toy models that reveal two complementary visions and provide quantitative access to universal scaling: i) a discrete-time dynamic in which each time step corresponds to multiplication by a Gaussian random matrix; ii) weak continuous-time monitoring that induces a Dyson brownian motion of the eigenvalues of the density matrix. The first approach provides an algebraic characterization based on rotational invariance emerging in Kraus's operator space, focusing in particular on the unitary and orthogonal cases, respectively $\beta=2$ and $\beta=1$, with $\beta$ the Dyson random-matrix index. The second approach, on the other hand, allows for a unified treatment for any $\beta$, thanks to the mapping of the Fokker-Planck evolution of eigenvalues onto the Calogero-Sutherland integrable Hamiltonian diagonalized in terms of Jack polynomials. We provide explicit expressions for the universal decrease of R\'enyi entropies. We show that, approaching the universal scaling limit, numerical simulations of different models agree with each other and with our theoretical predictions. Our results clarify the existence of different classes of universality for the purification process in hybrid quantum systems, accessible in random circuit architectures and weak measurement protocols.
item.dc:creator: Federico Gerbino, Donghoon Kim, Guido Giachetti, Andrea De Luca, Xhek Turkeshi

item.title: Bootstrapping Fermionic $R$-operators with Decorated Yang--Baxter Equations
item.description: arXiv:2603.11172v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrating infinitesimal generators of local dynamics into finite-time evolution is generally harder than extracting a local Hamiltonian from a quantum gate. For integrable one-dimensional quantum many-body systems, a recent bootstrap constructs one-parameter $R$-operators directly from Hamiltonians satisfying the Reshetikhin condition. However, this condition excludes important models such as the Hubbard model, whose two-parameter $R$-operator was obtained by Shastry from a decorated Yang--Baxter equation obeyed by its free-fermion sector. Here, I extend the bootstrap to $R$-operators constrained by both the ordinary and decorated Yang--Baxter equations. Their joint expansion produces additional Hamiltonian-level necessary conditions and recursively determines candidate higher-order terms, subject to two-site locality at each order. I also derive compatibility and factorization conditions under which a Shastry-type superposition solves the $RLL$ relation after deformation by an onsite involution. The construction recovers the known two-parameter $R$-operators of the Hubbard and XYh models, whose full Yang--Baxter equations follow from established tetrahedral Zamolodchikov algebra relations. For a superconducting Hubbard deformation, the scalar equations are generically incompatible, placing it outside this framework. These results provide diagnostics and a systematic route to fermionic $R$-operators beyond the Reshetikhin condition. General sufficiency, convergence of the formal bootstrap, and sufficiency of the deformation conditions remain open.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Zhang

item.title: Algorithmic Locality of Quantum Tensor Network Belief Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2604.21919v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Belief propagation has recently emerged as a powerful framework for evaluating tensor networks in higher dimensions, combining computational efficiency with provable analytical guarantees. In this work, we develop the first end-to-end theory of tensor network belief propagation for a class of projected entangled pair states satisfying \emph{strong injectivity}. We show that when the injectivity parameter exceeds a constant threshold, BP fixed points can be found efficiently, and a cluster-corrected BP algorithm computes physical quantities to $1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$ error in $\mathrm{poly}(N)$ time for an $N$ qubit system. We further identify a striking phenomenon we term \emph{algorithmic locality}: local perturbations of the tensor network affect the BP fixed point with an influence decaying rapidly with distance. Moreover, through the cluster expansion, this locality extends to observables, implying that local expectation values can be approximated from local data with controlled accuracy. We exhibit three regimes admitting strong injectivity: random Gaussian PEPS with large physical dimension, high-temperature Gibbs states of commuting two-body Hamiltonians, and fixed-depth quantum circuits subject to sufficiently strong depolarizing noise. Our bounds are worst-case sufficient conditions and do not identify sharp algorithmic transitions.
item.dc:creator: Siddhant Midha, Yifan F. Zhang, Daniel Malz, Dmitry A. Abanin, Sarang Gopalakrishnan

item.title: Pole Skipping, Avoided Crossing, and Resonant Excitation in Kerr Quasinormal Modes near Algebraically Special Frequencies
item.description: arXiv:2605.17840v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kerr quasinormal modes near algebraically special frequencies exhibit anomalous behavior, including apparent bifurcation, disappearance, and a nonsmooth connection to the Schwarzschild limit, which has remained puzzling for decades. Tracking poles and zeros of Green-function building blocks across different Riemann sheets, we show that the bifurcation is due to an avoided crossing accompanied by resonant excitation, while the disappearance is due to pole skipping caused by cancellation of a quasinormal-mode pole by a Matsubara-mode zero. This resolves the physical origin of these long-standing anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Kei-ichiro Kubota, Hayato Motohashi

item.title: The bulk spectral gap is certifiable from above but uncomputable from below
item.description: arXiv:2606.03836v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Determining spectral gaps in the thermodynamic limit is a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. When a fixed boundary condition is imposed, this problem is undecidable: no algorithm, even with unlimited resources, can decide for every Hamiltonian whether it is gapped. Yet the thermodynamic limit is meant to capture the intrinsic properties of very large systems, which should not depend on how their boundaries are chosen. We therefore consider the bulk spectral gap, which concerns only the intrinsic excitations of the infinite system, and ask what can and cannot be computed about it. First, we give a general algorithm producing a hierarchy of certified upper bounds on the bulk gap, arbitrarily tight at the cost of more computation. Second, we prove that the spectral gap problem remains undecidable in the bulk, already for translationally invariant nearest-neighbour chains of fixed local dimension. Hence no general algorithm produces convergent lower bounds, and no convergent upper-bounding algorithm, ours included, admits a computable convergence rate. The bulk spectral gap is thus certifiable from above but uncomputable from below; more precisely, the bulk-gaplessness promise problem is RE-complete, exactly as hard as the halting problem. The same construction shows that no general algorithm can decide whether a given product state is a ground state, and that convergent bounds on ground-state expectation values admit no computable convergence rate in general. Finally, we obtain the first nontrivial certified upper bounds on the bulk gap of the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.
item.dc:creator: Xiangling Xu, Matthias Sch\"otz, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Igor Klep, Omar Fawzi, Marc-Olivier Renou

item.title: Structural Chirality from Short-Range Order in Heteroanionic Materials
item.description: arXiv:2608.04841v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Established routes to structural chirality in inorganic crystals predominantly depend on symmetry-lowering atomic displacements of an achiral parent structure. We show that chirality can instead be forced by the short-range order of two anion species over the sites of an achiral parent, independent of atomic displacements. ReO$_3$-type oxyfluorides with a 2:1 anion stoichiometry, such as NbO$_2$F, exhibit two ordering patterns, cis octahedral coordination and period-three anion-chain ordering, both of which are rooted in the off-centring of $d^0$ cations. By direct enumeration, we prove that every arrangement combining both orderings on the smallest commensurate cell is chiral, belonging to a Sohncke space group. For NbO$_2$F, density-functional theory (DFT) calculations predict a homochiral $P3_121$ ground state. Wang-Landau Monte Carlo simulations of a DFT-trained cluster-expansion model predict that the chiral phase remains the equilibrium state up to a first-order transition at 494 K. We also identify three known vacancy-ordered compounds, BaZnO$_2$, BaCoO$_2$ and $\beta$-Fe$_2$SeO, whose structures each map onto one of the enumerated chiral arrangements. Together, these results establish short-range order as a route to structural chirality, and mark heteroanionic and vacancy-ordered materials in which both orderings are active as candidates for new chiral phases.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin J. Morgan

item.title: Criteria for Feasible Monte Carlo Stochastic Simulations of Bosonic Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2608.06056v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Monte Carlo sampling of the stochastic differential equations (SDEs) based on the quasiprobability distribution function, such as the Glauber--Sudarshan P, Wigner, and Husimi Q functions provides a powerful framework for investigating bosonic open quantum many-body dynamics described by the Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) equation, while considering the effects of quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field approximation. However, the stochastic Monte Carlo simulation is possible only when the corresponding Fokker--Planck equation has a positive-semidefinite diffusion matrix, and the general conditions for the diffusion matrix to be positive semidefinite have remained unclear. In this work, starting from the path integral formulation, we first derive the sufficient conditions under which the diffusion matrix is positive semidefinite for an arbitrary Hamiltonian, jump operators, and choice of quasiprobability distribution functions. We also analytically derive the corresponding SDEs to be solved. We then investigate the dynamics of the GKSL equation in the thermodynamic limit and show that, depending on the form of the jump operators, the mean-field approximation may fail to describe the dynamics accurately, making stochastic Monte Carlo simulations indispensable. Furthermore, we derive the sufficient conditions under which the higher-order quantum fluctuation terms beyond the Fokker--Planck description vanish identically, even when the jump operators contain quadratic terms. Under these conditions, whenever the corresponding SDEs can be derived, the stochastic Monte Carlo simulation reproduces the exact dynamics. These results clarify the conditions under which the stochastic Monte Carlo simulations are both feasible and necessary for accurately describing the dynamics governed by the GKSL equation in phase space.
item.dc:creator: Toma Yoneya, Kazuya Fujimoto, Yuki Kawaguchi

item.title: Explosive Synchronization in Inertial Kuramoto Models: Determining Resilience in Power Grids
item.description: arXiv:2609.00910v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Maintaining power-grid stability is essential for a sustainable energy supply. Using empirical power-grid data, we show that the inertial Kuramoto model with correlated powers and coupling strengths provides a relevant framework for analyzing explosive synchronization and grid stability. We identify two distinct synchronization pathways, initiated by population-driven or coupling-driven seed rotors, that yield different order-parameter behaviors. Inertia, in turn, determines whether the resulting seed clusters retain distinct angular velocities. Similar mechanisms govern recovery from external disturbances, linking power-grid resilience to these two nucleation pathways. Our findings provide a microscopic framework for understanding synchronization and recovery, with implications for stable power-grid operation.
item.dc:creator: Cook Hyun Kim, Jihye Kim, Sangjoon Park, J\"urgen Kurths, B. Kahng

item.title: Redundant Records of the Past: Unifying Quantum Darwinism and Decoherent Histories
item.description: arXiv:2610.09845v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: There exist two different paradigms for records in isolated quantum systems: decoherent histories (which determines which past events leave formal records) and quantum Darwinism (which determines which current events get redundantly recorded). Neither one implies the other, and connections between the two are scarcely investigated. We unify quantum Darwinism and decoherent histories based on the insight that only redundant records about past events matter. The resulting framework of past redundancy encompasses quantum Darwinism when applied to events at the current time, and it implies the probability sum rule or decoherence of histories. The Bhattacharyya coefficient (or fidelity) plays an important role to establish this connection. Importantly, various examples show that past redundancy is a more widespread phenomenon than the fine-tuned models necessary for quantum Darwinism suggest. We thus arrive at a richer picture in which redundancy can be caused by mechanisms different from quantum Darwinism (such as macroevents or cascade structures), which emphasizes that redundancy is necessary but not sufficient for objectivity, and which, overall, allows to realistically investigate the question: how generic is redundancy in nature?
item.dc:creator: Philipp Strasberg

item.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
item.description: arXiv:2610.12929v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.
item.dc:creator: David C. Newsom, Michael Levin

item.title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
item.description: arXiv:2610.21478v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW model, enforcing the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. The preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries is compatible only with the pairing condition.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiki Fukusumi, Shuma Nakashiba

item.title: From Action Principle to Stochastic Thermodynamics of Elastic and Viscous Active Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.21835v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the complex material properties of living matter, we derive a framework of stochastic thermo- and elastodynamics for active materials from the classical principle of least action and the Rayleighian formalism for external forces. Our approach couples the local barycentric collective coordinate and the streaming velocity as the canonical conjugate pair, which unifies various descriptions of elastic and viscous soft matter, including Helfrich theory for lipid membranes, linear and nonlinear elasticity of thin shells and deformable droplets, as well as hydrodynamics of active and passive fluids. The Lagrangian mechanics of collective field variables permits direct applications of the results and theorems from statistical mechanics to existing models of complex soft and living matter. To illustrate the potential applications of stochastic elastodynamics in biology, we derive and simulate a boundary-driven deformation model of an elastic cell nucleus in the presence of fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Valentina Barletta, Michele Lupini, Ian D. Estabrook, Laeschkir W\"urthner, Isabella R. Graf, Caren Norden, Lamberto Rondoni, Anna Erzberger, Roman Belousov
